sections.name: TaskTimeline
sections.title: Timeline bars for each task
sections.what: Draws a card with a heading and one row per task. Each row shows the title, a status badge that is green for completed, amber for doing and gray otherwise, and the estimate. A bar under each row grows with the estimate up to 120 minutes, with a short minimum and a full-width maximum.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed 120-minute scale makes the bars easy to compare at a glance.
sections.watch_out: Any task longer than 120 minutes shows the same full-width bar, so very long tasks cannot be told apart.

summary: Shows each task as a row with a bar whose length reflects its estimated minutes.
purpose: Give a rough visual comparison of how long each task is expected to take.
why: Likely reason: a bar per task is a simple stand-in for a schedule, and no dates are used here, so it is not a true calendar timeline.
how: 1. Receives the task list from its parent. 2. For each task, works out a bar width from its estimate, with a minimum and a maximum. 3. Draws the title, a status badge and the estimate, with the bar underneath. 4. Shows a note when the list is empty.
inputs: A list of tasks, using their titles, statuses and time estimates.
outputs: A card of bars on screen. Nothing is saved.
risks: The bar scale stops at 120 minutes. The empty message says there are no active tasks, but completed tasks may still be shown.
debug: If a bar looks wrong, check that the task's estimate is a number. If bars all look equal, check the 120-minute scale. If the list is missing tasks, check the filter used by the parent.
